=== daily-publish.yml:
# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'
        type: choice
        default: none
        options:
          - none
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - website
          - addin

permissions:
  contents: read

# One daily at a time; a queued run must not cancel an in-flight one.
concurrency:
  group: daily-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  plan:
    name: Plan (change detection + versions)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # gh-1477: 10m was the same time bomb as the derive-version jobs — a
    # full-history fetch under a 10m ceiling. 20m + the blobless filter
    # below.

build-android:
    name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle
      # died on "No file or variants found for asset: .env"). Content mirrors
      # the ci.yml/build-macos.yml incantation — bare `touch` is not enough
      # on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist step: the committed
      # google-services.json is a placeholder (the google-services Gradle
      # plugin hard-fails without the file); overwrite it from the secret
      # when available.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written (package: $(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json'))['client'][0]['client_info']['android_client_info']['package_name'])"))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      - name: Validate Android secrets
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            echo "::error::PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON secret is not set — the Play Developer API service-account JSON key is required"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          if [ -z "$ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS" ]; then echo "::error::ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS secret is not set"; exit 1; fi
          echo "All required Android secrets are present"

      - name: Setup Ruby
        # ubuntu-24.04 runner images ship no Ruby — `bundle: command not
        # found` exit 127 (issue #353). Same setup as store-metadata.yml.
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@de492cf36cbab201753d720ce4f4e336cd688c94 # v1.328.0 (branch head; v1 moves)
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.2'

      - name: Install fastlane
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: bundle install

      # gh-1655: same NDK pre-install as ci.yml build-android — the
      # release lane's Gradle configuration auto-installs the
      # Flutter-pinned NDK mid-build with no retry; one truncated
      # download reds the lane. Bounded-retry pre-install instead.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall

      # The lane wraps `flutter build appbundle --release`; the upload
      # keystore rides the ANDROID_* env vars (issue #289) and is decoded
      # by app/build.gradle.kts into the (gitignored) build dir — no
      # key.properties dance. ANDROID_STRICT_RELEASE_SIGNING makes a
      # secret-less release build fail LOUDLY instead of debug-signing.
      - name: Build Android AAB
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          # gh-1522: the AAB's versionName rides the derived tag version
          # (BUILD_NAME) — the committed pubspec is the static 0.0.0-dev
          # placeholder and never churns. BUILD_NUMBER stays the run number
          # (Play versionCode).
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_STRICT_RELEASE_SIGNING: 'true'
        run: bundle exec fastlane android build_release

      - name: Verify AAB and validate bundle
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          AAB_PATH="flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab"
          if [ ! -f "$AAB_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::AAB file not found at $AAB_PATH"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "AAB built successfully: $(ls -la $AAB_PATH)"
          # bundletool validate (issue #289 AC3): catches malformed bundles
          # before they ever reach Play's upload pipeline.
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o /tmp/bundletool.jar \
            https://github.com/google/bundletool/releases/download/1.17.0/bundletool-all-1.17.0.jar
          java -jar /tmp/bundletool.jar validate --bundle "$AAB_PATH"
          echo "✅ bundletool validate green"
          # 16 KB page-size gate (gh-746, review round 1): re-check every
          # native lib in the PACKAGED bundle — a staging-layout change that
          # silently un-wires the gate fails here instead of at Play upload.
          # The gate lives in its own script so aab-gate-selftest.yml runs
          # the SAME logic against fixture bundles on every PR (gh-798 AC3):
          # AAB layout base/lib/<abi>/*.so, owned named verdict — never an
          # inherited exit code (gh-786).
          bash scripts/verify_aab_native_libs.sh "$AAB_PATH"

      - name: Upload AAB Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: android-aab
          path: flutter_app/build/app/outputs/bundle/storeRelease/app-store-release.aab
          retention-days: 14

  submit-android:
    name: Submit Android to Play
    needs: [build-android]

So the fix: add the same cache step to build-mobile.yml's Android jobs — covering BOTH roots. The cache path can list both `flutter_app/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared` and `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared` (actions/cache supports multi-path).

But caching alone leaves the first run (cache-miss) exposed — exactly the state we're in NOW: there's no cache to restore yet for build-mobile. The ci.yml cache exists but is keyed to the ROOT package's dir — different path, so it can't seed the flutter_app one... Actually actions/cache restore-keys are scoped to the repo+branch; path differs but key namespace is shared. We could restore the ci.yml-seded cache... but the CONTENT of root `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared` vs `flutter_app/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared` — both are `download-<hash8>/libsqlite3.so` dirs. The hash8 is the same across roots IF the sqlite3 version matches (hash8 = first 8 chars of the asset hash — same asset = same dirname). The saved filename differs per target OS (`libsqlite3.so` for android AND linux — same name!). Actually for android: `libraryFileName('sqlite3', DynamicLoadingBundled())` → Android OS → `libsqlite3.so`. For linux host: also `libsqlite3.so`. Same dirname → IDENTICAL layout!

Wait, is that safe? The linux x64 `libsqlite3.so` vs android x64 `libsqlite3.so` — dirname = `download-<hash8-of-asset>` — hash8 differs per asset (different files: `libsqlite3.x64.linux.so` hash vs `libsqlite3.x64.android.so` hash). So dirs don't collide: `download-037539c6/...` etc. The dirname is content-addressed — cross-root cache sharing is safe as long as the sqlite3 package version (its asset_hashes table) agrees.

Hmm OK. But hold on — is a CI-cache-only fix the right "minimum targeted fix" for this bug? Let me reconsider.

The bug: transient GitHub release-asset brownout (504 HTML body hashed) breaks three build-mobile jobs. The repo ALREADY had this exact incident on 2026-09-21 and fixed it in ci.yml with a cache. The play leg (build-mobile.yml) was NOT covered by that fix and now broke the same way (2026-11-09). The clear, minimal, pattern-following fix: **extend the same hooks-shared cache protection to build-mobile.yml's Android jobs** (and arguably the iOS job too, but scope = the failing leg; iOS builds also use sqlite3 native assets? flutter_app iOS — yes it would, but let me check which jobs the leg runs — android_content=all; testflight runs ios. The ticket only covers play leg. But the same latent risk exists in the iOS jobs and emulator IT jobs. Minimal fix = the failing play-leg jobs: build-android (AB) + build-android-apks (god/store matrix). Hmm — but also `test-android-emulator` runs for android legs (needs build-android-apks artifacts — it installs prebuilt APKs, no rebuild... actually it uses the built APK artifact, so no hook runs there unless it builds... let me check briefly).

Additionally, caching only helps after the FIRST successful download. To make even the first run robust, add a **retry pre-warm**: run `flutter build` — no. Better: a bounded-retry download that seeds the cache before the build, like the `android-ndk-preinstall` action pattern (gh-165: "one truncated download reds the lane. Bounded-retry pre-install instead."). There's an established repo pattern: `.github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall` — bounded-retry pre-install of the NDK. The analogous fix: an action/script that pre-warms the sqlite3 hook cache with bounded retries.

Hmm, wait. Let me not over-enginer. Let me think about what's most robust and minimal:

**Option 1 (cache only)**: Add actions/cache of hooks-shared dirs to the build-mobile Android jobs. Matches ci.yml precedent exactly. Weakness: on a cache miss (first run, or cache eviction, or version bump changing the asset), the download still happens and can still brown out → red leg again. The current run has no cache seeded for these paths → the NEXT run would still fail... unless ci.yml's cache seeded the same dirs. Different paths, so no.

Actually wait — I need to check WHICH pub cache version build-mobile uses. flutter_app/pubspec.lock pins sqlite3 3.7.0 (path-dep root → flutter_app resolves its own lock). The root pubspec resolves ^3.5.1 → 3.9.1 (latest). So build-mobile needs: android assets for sqlite3-3.7.0 (AB + APK builds in flutter_app) AND root-host assets for 3.9.1 (assert-builtin-skills dart run at root).

Hmm hold on — which sqlite3 does the root package build hooks use when running on the Linux host? The root pub cache in CI had sqlite3-3.9.1 (the AB failure shows pub-cache path sqlite3-3.9.1 with root .dart_tool). And flutter_app build used sqlite3-3.7.0 (its own lockfile).

**Option 2 (cache + bounded-retry pre-warm)**: Add a pre-warm step that downloads the needed sqlite3 release assets with `curl --retry` (retry survives the brownout) into the hooks-shared cache layout, then the cache step persists them for future runs. The pre-warm needs the exact dirname/filename mapping:
- dirname = `download-<first 8 hex of asset sha256>`
- asset file = `libsqlite3.<arch>.<os>.so` from `https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases/download/sqlite3-<pkg-version>/<asset>`
- saved as `libsqlite3.so` inside the dirname.

But which arches does a build need? For Android AB/APK builds: arm, arm64, ia32, x64 (all 4 android ABIs per `_supportedAbis.android`); flutter builds target all release ABIs by default (arm32? flutter's default android ABIs = arm32-v7a, arm64-v8a, x86_64 — x86? the release build for play typically excludes x86... The hook builds for the ABIs gradle requests: armeabi-v7a(arm), arm64-v8a(arm64), x86(ia32)?, x86_64(x64). flutter gradle default: armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a, x86_64 for release app? Actually `flutter build apk --release` defaults to all three: armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a, x86_64. Hmm ia32 (x86) is NOT in flutter's default. So 3 ABIs. And the root-package dart run needs linux x64.

Maintaining a pre-warm script that knows (version, tag, asset list, hash8s, expected hashes) duplicates the package's asset_hashes data — brittle: every sqlite3 bump would need script updates... UNLESS the script DERIVES the data from the pub cache (read `asset_hashes.dart` from the resolved sqlite3 package in pub cache!). That's doable: a small script that:
1. Finds the resolved sqlite3 package dir (from `.dart_tool/package_config.json` — for both root and flutter_app).
2. Parses `lib/src/hook/asset_hashes.dart` (releaseTag + map).
3. For each needed (os, arch) pair, computes dirname + source filename, checks whether the target file already exists in the cache; if not, downloads with curl --retry and verifies the sha256, then writes it.

Hmm — but wait, this is getting complex. Let me reconsider: is there a SIMPLER, more hermetic fix the repo could own?

**Option 3: Make the hook read from a local directory** — `source: test-sqlite3` + `directory:` user-define in `flutter_app/hook/build.yaml`... requires vendoring ALL android assets in-repo (~9MB) AND the linux one for root tests (~2MB). Commiting ~11MB binaries. Also `PrecompiledForTesting` is documented "only used to test the package". Too invasive.

**Option 4: Just retry the whole failing step with a bounded-retry wrapper.** The brownout is intermittent; ci.yml precedent for mid-build flaky downloads is the NDK pre-install action (bounded retry). For flutter builds, a retry of the whole `flutter build appbundle` after a hooks failure is cheap ONLY if the failure happens early (14.6s in for AB — the hook fails fast). A retry-loop around the fastlane build would eventually pass once GitHub recovers... but each retry re-downloads (no cache) → wasted bandwidth, still 504-exposed, and slow lanes. Meh.

**Best fix = Option 2 (cache + pre-warm with bounded retry), implemented as a composite action following the repo's established patterns.** Actually — wait. Let me check if the repo already HAS such an action or script for this (the ci.yml comment mentions the 2026-09-21 fix; maybe there's an action). Let me search .github/actions/ and scripts/ for hooks/sqlite prewarm.

Also — maybe simpler and fully within pattern: the ci.yml cache pattern ALONE plus `restore-keys` cross-seding. Hmm, the build-mobile jobs could restore from a key that ci.yml writes... but paths differ (root vs flutter_app). Actions/cache allows restoring a cache saved under a different key (restore-keys prefix match) but the PATH argument determines what gets downloaded into the workspace. The cache archive contains files relative to the `path:` used at save time. If ci.yml saves path `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared`, restoring it into build-mobile with `path: flutter_app/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared` would... place files under flutter_app/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared — actually YES, actions/cache just extracts the archive at the given path. The archive stores the subtree under `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared`; restoring to a different path extracts it there. So a build-mobile cache entry with `key: hooks-shared-...-flutter_app-...` + `restore-keys: hooks-shared-Linux-X64-` would pick up ci.yml's root cache and extract it into flutter_app/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared. The dirname/filename layout is identical (content-addressed), so this WORKS for the android ABIs ci.yml already downloaded... but ci.yml's root cache contains LINUX assets (dart test on ubuntu host), not ANDROID assets! dirname for android x64 (`download-<hash8 android asset>`) ≠ linux x64. So cross-seding gives nothing for android builds. Only `assert-builtin-skills`' root linux download would benefit.

OK so decision: implement a pre-warm script + cache in build-mobile.yml. Let me look at how `android-ndk-preinstall` is written to follow the repo's action conventions, and check the flutter-pub-get composite action (maybe the pre-warm belongs THERE — it runs in every Android job right before builds! That would cover AB, APK matrix, emulator IT jobs, and iOS if flutter-pub-get is shared).

===
name: 'Flutter pub get (enforced lockfile, bounded retry)'
description: >-
  The ONE sanctioned flutter_app dependency-resolution step:
  `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` with the #726 bounded retry. pub
  has no retry for its git-dependency mirror clones (flutter_js,
  flutter_js_widget_runtime) — one transient "Connection reset by peer" on
  github.com:443 failed the whole leg (#726 on the iOS release leg; gh-1310
  on ci.yml build-macos, where the v1.0.516 lockfile refresh cold-missed
  the flutter-action pub cache and forced fresh clones exactly when a
  release lands). Deterministic pubspec/lockfile skews (gh-1299: a release
  commit that bumps the version without regenerating flutter_app/
  pubspec.lock) fail identically on every attempt — the loop detects the
  "Unable to satisfy" signature and fails fast instead of burning ~30s per
  red leg and blaming the network (PR #1268 review thread 3). Guarded by
  test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test.dart: no workflow run-step may resolve
  flutter_app itself.

inputs:
  working-directory:
    description: 'Directory holding the pubspec.yaml to resolve.'
    required: false
    default: flutter_app

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile (bounded retry, #726)
      working-directory: ${{ inputs.working-directory }}
      env:
        # Git-dep clones must never hang a leg on a credential prompt.
        GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        LOG_FILE="$(mktemp)"
        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          # gh-1265 AC2: resolve against the committed lockfile.
          if flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_FILE"; then
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 0
          fi
          # A pubspec/lockfile skew is deterministic — retrying cannot
          # fix it, so fail fast instead of burning ~30s per red leg and
          # blaming the network (PR #1268 review thread 3).
          if grep -qE 'Unable to satisfy .* using .*pubspec\.lock' "$LOG_FILE"; then
            echo "::error::$PWD/pubspec.lock is out of sync with $PWD/pubspec.yaml — regenerate it (cd $PWD && flutter pub get) and commit; not retrying a deterministic skew"
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$attempt" = 3 ]; then
            echo "::error::flutter pub get failed after 3 attempts — the runner's network to pub.dev/github.com is unhealthy"
            rm -f "$LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "::warning::flutter pub get failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 15s"
          sleep 15
        done
=== ndk:
name: android-ndk-preinstall
description: >-
  Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK and the AGP-default CMake so
  Gradle configuration never triggers an on-demand sdkmanager download
  mid-build. gh-1655: one truncated android-ndk-r28c-linux download
  ("Error on ZipFile unknown archive" at 33%) red'd the ci.yml build-android
  leg — and the aggregate Quality gate with it — because AGP's
  in-configuration auto-install path has NO retry. gh-1757: the same leg
  died the same way on the sibling component — the `:jni` module
  (transitive `jni` package via path_provider_android) wires
  externalNativeBuild.cmake with no version, so AGP auto-installs its
  default cmake;3.22.1 mid-configuration and one corrupt archive
  ("Archive is not a ZIP archive") red'd v1.0.619's build-android leg, the
  aggregate Quality gate, and the Advance vpinned marker job with it. The
  NDK version is resolved from the pinned Flutter SDK's own gradle plugin
  source (the exact value flutter.ndkVersion resolves to — no second pin
  to drift), the CMake version is the AGP default cross-checked against
  the AGP pin by the guard test, both installs are skipped when the
  component is already present, and each download is bounded-retried —
  the same hardening the (since-removed) flutter_gemma Android seed
  carried (gh-1468).
  Companion guard: test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Pre-install the Flutter-pinned Android NDK + AGP-default CMake (bounded retry)
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        # flutter.ndkVersion's single source of truth: the gradle plugin
        # bundled with the SDK flutter-action installed. app/
        # build.gradle.kts reads `ndkVersion = flutter.ndkVersion`, so
        # resolving here can never skew from what AGP requests at
        # configuration time (a literal pin on either side would break
        # that coupling — the guard test pins both sides).
        if [ -n "${FLUTTER_ROOT:-}" ]; then
          FLUTTER_HOME="$FLUTTER_ROOT"
        else
          FLUTTER_BIN="$(command -v flutter || true)"
          if [ -z "$FLUTTER_BIN" ]; then
            echo "::error::cannot locate flutter (set FLUTTER_ROOT) — the NDK pre-install resolves the version from the SDK's gradle plugin source"
            exit 1
          fi
          FLUTTER_HOME="$(dirname "$(dirname "$FLUTTER_BIN")")"
        fi
        GRADLE_SRC="$FLUTTER_HOME/packages/flutter_tools/gradle/src/main/kotlin/FlutterExtension.kt"
        NDK_VERSION="$(grep -hoE 'val ndkVersion: String = "[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+"' "$GRADLE_SRC" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)"
        if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "::error::cannot resolve flutter.ndkVersion from $GRADLE_SRC — the Flutter gradle plugin layout moved; update the extraction in .github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall (and test/ci_android_ndk_preinstall_guard_test.dart) TOGETHER"
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "resolved flutter.ndkVersion = $NDK_VERSION"
        ANDROID_SDK="${ANDROID_HOME:-/usr/local/lib/android/sdk}"
        SDKMANAGER="$ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
        if [ ! -x "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          SDKMANAGER="$(command -v sdkmanager || true)"
        fi
        if [ -z "$SDKMANAGER" ]; then
          echo "::error::sdkmanager not found (expected $ANDROID_SDK/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager) — the NDK pre-install needs the Android cmdline-tools"
          exit 1
        fi
        # Idempotence: AGP resolves `ndkVersion` against
        # $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/<version> — source.properties present means
        # the NDK is fully installed. gh-1757: the same Gradle
        # configuration step also provisions CMake — the `:jni` module
        # (transitive `jni` package via path_provider_android) wires
        # externalNativeBuild.cmake with no version, so AGP falls back
        # to its default 3.22.1 (the AGP pin lives in
        # flutter_app/android/settings.gradle.kts; the guard test
        # cross-checks the coupling) and auto-installs it
        # mid-configuration with no retry when
        # $ANDROID_HOME/cmake/<version> is missing. Both lookups mirror
        # exactly what AGP performs: a provisioned component means the
        # pre-install is a no-op.
        NEEDS_NDK=1
        if [ -f "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION/source.properties" ]; then
          echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          NEEDS_NDK=0
        fi
        CMAKE_VERSION="3.22.1"
        NEEDS_CMAKE=1
        if [ -x "$ANDROID_SDK/cmake/$CMAKE_VERSION/bin/cmake" ]; then
          echo "CMake $CMAKE_VERSION already installed — skipping pre-install"
          NEEDS_CMAKE=0
        fi
        if [ "$NEEDS_NDK" = "0" ] && [ "$NEEDS_CMAKE" = "0" ]; then
          echo "NDK and CMake already provisioned — nothing to pre-install"
          exit 0
        fi
        # Accept any license the image has not pre-accepted so the
        # installs below never prompt (|| true: `yes` dies of SIGPIPE by
        # design once sdkmanager stops reading).
        yes | "$SDKMANAGER" --licenses > /dev/null || true
        # gh-1655: Gradle's own auto-install (the same sdkmanager call,
        # run inside configuration) has no retry — one truncated download
        # unzips as "Error on ZipFile unknown archive" and the build dies.
        # Here the same download gets three attempts with backoff.
        # gh-1757 first: CMake is the smaller download and the failure
        # v1.0.619 actually hit (`:jni:configureCMakeDebug`).
        if [ "$NEEDS_CMAKE" = "1" ]; then
          CMAKE_OK=0
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            echo "installing CMake $CMAKE_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
            rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/cmake/$CMAKE_VERSION"
            if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "cmake;$CMAKE_VERSION" && [ -x "$ANDROID_SDK/cmake/$CMAKE_VERSION/bin/cmake" ]; then
              echo "CMake $CMAKE_VERSION installed"
              CMAKE_OK=1
              break
            fi
            echo "::warning::sdkmanager CMake install failed or bin/cmake missing (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$CMAKE_OK" = "0" ]; then
            echo "::error::CMake $CMAKE_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1757: the :jni module auto-installs it mid-build with no retry, and one corrupt archive (\"Archive is not a ZIP archive\") red'd v1.0.619's build-android leg; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
            exit 1
          fi
        fi
        if [ "$NEEDS_NDK" = "1" ]; then
          NDK_OK=0
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            echo "installing NDK $NDK_VERSION (attempt $attempt/3)"
            rm -rf "$ANDROID_SDK/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
            if "$SDKMANAGER" --install "ndk;$NDK_VERSION"; then
              echo "NDK $NDK_VERSION installed"
              NDK_OK=1
              break
            fi
            echo "::warning::sdkmanager NDK install failed (attempt $attempt/3) — retrying in 10s"
            sleep 10
          done
          if [ "$NDK_OK" = "0" ]; then
            echo "::error::NDK $NDK_VERSION install failed after 3 attempts — gh-1655 red'd the leg on a single truncated archive; inspect the sdkmanager output above"
            exit 1
          fi
        fi

build-android-apks:
    # Issue #622: the flavor matrix. The AAB job above stays the Play
    # pipeline (store, unchanged); this job builds BOTH release APKs from
    # ONE variable — FLAVOR drives both the gradle --flavor and the
    # FA_FLAVOR dart-define (contract: the pair must never drift). god
    # (applicationId dev.fa1.app.god) is sideload-only and NEVER reaches
    # Play (binding threat model): it ships as an APK attached to the
    # GitHub release. store keeps its AAB for Play and additionally gets
    # an APK for direct installs + the UT-CI-1 size-delta tracking.
    name: Build Android APK (${{ matrix.flavor }})
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        flavor: [store, god]
    env:
      FLAVOR: ${{ matrix.flavor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # Same placeholder-.env incantation as build-android (issue #368):
      # .env is a declared Flutter asset and newer flutter validates
      # assets at build time.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors build-android, gated to the store flavor: the secret file
      # carries ONLY the dev.fa1.app client, while the god applicationId is
      # dev.fa1.app.god — overwriting it would hard-fail the google-services
      # plugin ("No matching client found for package name
      # 'dev.fa1.app.god'"). god builds with the committed placeholder
      # google-services.json, which carries both clients.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ "$FLAVOR" != "store" ]; then
            echo "$FLAVOR builds with the committed placeholder google-services.json — the secret file has no dev.fa1.app.god client"
          elif [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written"
          else
            echo "GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      # gh-1655: same NDK pre-install as ci.yml build-android — the
      # flavor matrix's Gradle configuration auto-installs the
      # Flutter-pinned NDK mid-build with no retry; one truncated
      # download reds the leg. Bounded-retry pre-install instead.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/android-ndk-preinstall

      # Same release keystore as the AAB job (contract: store and god sign
      # with the SAME release key — only the applicationId differs), same
      # strict-signing posture: no silent debug-signed APKs. No Play
      # service account here — god never touches Play.
      - name: Build flavor APK
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          # gh-1522: stamp the APK version strings from the derived tag
          # version — the committed pubspec is the static 0.0.0-dev
          # placeholder and never churns.
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}

=== emulator job:
  test-android-emulator:
    # Issue #622 (card DoD): emulator CI job shape for the six mobile
    # channel integration tests (flutter_app/test/integration/
    # mobile_channel_it.dart, tagged `integration`):
    #   IT-flavor-1  — release-manifest audit per flavor
    #   IT-floor-1   — mobile.* availability per tier (issue #19 floor)
    #   IT-observe-1 — hierarchy + screenshot over the channel
    #   IT-gesture-1 — tap / swipe / text injection
    #   IT-shell-1   — Shizuku round-trip (god + opt-in bridge)
    #   IT-consent-1 — consent flow + one-tap disable
    # DISABLED with `if: false` until an emulator runner is provisioned —
    # the hosted pool does not guarantee KVM and a red matrix would gate
    # every release. When provisioned: add
    # `needs: [version, build-android-apks]`, flip the `if` below to
    # `needs.build-android-apks.result == 'success'`, add a
    # download-artifact step for `android-apk-${{ matrix.flavor }}` before
    # the emulator boot, and the job goes green as-is. The same ONE-var
    # rule applies: FLAVOR drives --flavor and FA_FLAVOR.
    name: Android emulator ITs (${{ matrix.flavor }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: false
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        flavor: [store, god]
    env:
      FLAVOR: ${{ matrix.flavor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Boot emulator
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          test -e /dev/kvm || { echo "::error::/dev/kvm missing — the provisioned runner must expose KVM"; exit 1; }
          echo no | "$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/avdmanager" create avd \
            -n fa-it --package "system-images;android-34;google_apis;x86_64" --device pixel_5
          "$ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator" -avd fa-it \
            -no-window -no-audio -no-boot-anim -no-snapshot -accel on &
          adb wait-for-device
          until [ "$(adb shell getprop sys.boot_completed 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')" = "1" ]; do
            sleep 5
          done
          echo "Emulator booted"

      - name: Install flavor APK
        run: adb install -r "flutter_app/build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-$FLAVOR-release.apk"

      - name: Run mobile channel IT suite
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: flutter test test/integration/mobile_channel_it.dart --tags integration

  build-ios:
    name: Build iOS IPA
    needs: version
    # gh-1906: route to the shared `macos-m5` POOL. The gh-1692 pin of the
    # ONE known-good box (`fa-m5-1` runner-name label) is dead — no m5
    # runner carries a runner-name label anymore, so a set containing one
    # matched ZERO runners and both iOS legs queued forever (live
    # 2026-10-26, blocked v1.0.648 TestFlight). The gh-1692 fa-m5-2
    # signing-env concern is retired: fa-m5-2/fa-m5-3 signed desktop green.
    # The generic [self-hosted, macOS, ARM64] list stays banned (gh-1600
    # F-A: it also matches the Linux box) — see
    # test/workflow_selfhosted_legs_test.dart, which audits this exact
    # label set and bans `fa-m5-*` name labels repo-wide.
    runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5]
    # Issue #344: a wedged self-hosted worker (lost completion report)
    # otherwise holds the slot AND the in_progress status until the 300m
    # daily-publish watcher times out; a job-level timeout lets GitHub
    # fail the run server-side and unblock the pool + watchers.
    timeout-minutes: 90
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.ios_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Update local git mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
          # gh-1644: shared resilient updater — fetch retries + blobless
          # recreate with partial-dir cleanup (was single-shot; run
          # 38855793382 died exit 128 on a mid-clone network drop).
          # gh-1665 review: first step of the job, before any checkout —
          # the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree, so bootstrap the
          # script from the commit-pinned raw URL (mirror copy as the
          # no-network fallback), never from $GITHUB_WORKSPACE.
          SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
          RAW="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
          if ! curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 "$RAW" -o "$SCRIPT" \
             || [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
            echo "raw bootstrap failed — syncing the mirror and falling back to its copy" >&2
            # gh-1665 review (returned IMPORTANT): in the one-run-wide
            # first-post-merge window the persistent mirror is still a
            # PRE-MERGE tree. Cheap single-shot ensure (bounded resilience
            # stays owned by $SCRIPT below) so the extraction that follows
            # succeeds on any runner that can reach github.com at all —

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# 16 KB page-size gate for the PACKAGED Android bundle (gh-746; layout fix +
# owned verdict in gh-786). Called by build-mobile.yml's "Verify AAB" step
# and self-tested in CI by aab-gate-selftest.yml against fixture bundles
# (gh-798 AC3) — keep the two fixture expectations in sync with this file.
#
# Usage: verify_aab_native_libs.sh <path-to-aab>
#
# The gate owns its verdict: it never rides unzip's exit code — after the
# extraction it checks what matched and prints a named pass/fail. Native
# libs are EXPECTED in the store bundle (libapp/libflutter/libwasm_run_dart
# + LiteRT/QNN), so zero matches is a packaging regression, not a skip.
set -euo pipefail

AAB_PATH="${1:?usage: verify_aab_native_libs.sh <path-to-aab>}"
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

TMP_LIBS="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_LIBS"' EXIT
# AAB layout: native libs live at base/lib/<abi>/*.so — 'lib/*' is the APK
# layout and matches nothing (gh-786).
unzip -o -q "$AAB_PATH" 'base/lib/*' -d "$TMP_LIBS" || true
LIB_COUNT=$(find "$TMP_LIBS" -type f -name '*.so' | wc -l)
if [ "$LIB_COUNT" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "::error::expected native libs at base/lib/*/*.so in the AAB, found none — packaging regression (gh-786)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Native libs in the bundle: $LIB_COUNT"
find "$TMP_LIBS" -type f -name '*.so' | sed "s|$TMP_LIBS/||"
dart "$SCRIPT_DIR/patch_elf_16k_alignment.dart" --check "$TMP_LIBS"
echo "✅ 16 KB alignment check green"

# Root Cause Analysis **Bug**: The daily-publish `play` leg (build-mobile.yml) went red on three jobs — Build Android AAB, Build Android APK (god), Build Android APK (store) — all failing inside `package:sqlite3`'s native-assets build hook with `build.dart returned with exit code: 255`. **Root cause**: `package:sqlite3`'s build hook downloads prebuilt `libsqlite3` binaries from `https://github.com/simolus3/sqlite3.dart/releases/download//` and verifies each download against the SHA-256 pinned in the package's `lib/src/hook/asset_hashes.dart`. The released hook versions in use here do NOT check the HTTP status code before hashing: - `sqlite3` 3.7.0 (pinned by `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`): `PrecompiledBinary.fetch` in `lib/src/hook/compile/description.dart` streams the response body straight into the hasher. - `sqlite3` 3.9.1 (root package, floating `^3.5.1`): has the upstream status check (commit c9668a8, "Fail fast on download errors") but NO retry. During a GitHub release-download brownout (HTTP 504/429 error pages), the hook hashed the ERROR PAGE BODY instead of the binary. `bef140a1a9694029153dca8c00b1750b9a5a764fb9db2dc68d7bb40e8a29e8a` is the SHA-256 of GitHub's 504 page (`

504 Gateway Time-out

…`) — a constant for every caller, which is exactly what the failing logs show: `Bad state: Hash of downloaded file libsqlite3.x64.android.so is bef140a1…, expected 949965f0…`. The release assets themselves are intact (verified: the pinned URL currently serves the expected hash `949965f0…`). Documented upstream: simolus3/sqlite3.dart#435/#436. **Impact**: Three build-mobile.yml Android jobs failed ~2 minutes apart (05:23:54 / 05:25:38), each on its own runner, each re-downloading the assets it needed with no cache and no retry: - Build Android AAB → died in the `assert-builtin-skills` gate: the root `dart run` executes build hooks for the whole package graph (root resolves sqlite3 3.9.1) and the `libsqlite3.x64.linux.so` download failed. - Build Android APK (god/store) → died in `Build flavor APK`: the flutter_app build (lockfile-pinned sqlite3 3.7.0) failed the `libsqlite3.x64.android.so` download. ci.yml fixed this exact failure class for itself on 2026-09-21 by caching `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared` (the comment in ci.yml names the same brownout signature) — but build-mobile.yml never got that protection, so the play leg is exposed on every run. **Fix approach**: Mirror the two established repo patterns for unretryable mid-build downloads: 1. A bounded-retry, hash-verified pre-warm of the hook's content-addressed cache (`/.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/sqlite3/build/download-/`) — the gh-1655/gh-1757 `android-ndk-preinstall` pattern applied to the sqlite3 release assets. New `scripts/sqlite3_hook_prewarm.dart` derives the release tag + pinned hashes from the RESOLVED sqlite3 package (no second pin to drift), checks the HTTP status before hashing (the exact check upstream added too), retries with backoff, and skips idempotently when the cache already holds the verified bytes. 2. `actions/cache` on both hooks-shared dirs in the two failing build-mobile.yml jobs, seeded by the pre-warm — the ci.yml 2026-09-21 pattern extended to the mobile lane. The root-package host asset is pre-warmed inside `assert-builtin-skills` (the step that failed first), the flutter_app android assets in the jobs after `flutter pub get`. **Previous attempt**: none — first leg failure of this signature on the play leg (ci.yml's 2026-09-21 cache fix predates it and covers only the root lane).

Both negative paths verified:
- 504 with honest status → retried 3x, failed loudly, cache empty.
- 200 + error-page body (the exact gh-2074 signature a proxy can produce) → hash gate refuses, cache empty, loud error naming got/expected hashes.

Action pins guard passes.

Wait — one detail on the 200-garbage case: it did NOT retry (the mismatch throw isn't caught by the retry loop — only HttpStatusException/Timeout/Socket/HttpException are). It failed immediately on attempt 1. Is that right? A hash mismatch on a 200 is deterministic for a given URL — retrying the same URL would give the same bytes (unless it's a partial-body race, where a retry COULD help). Hmm. The upstream issue's failure was a 504-with-body (status visible). The gh-2074 logs show the hash-mismatch signature because 3.7.0 doesn't check status. For MY script, a mismatch means the endpoint is serving wrong bytes deterministically — retrying once could ride out a mid-transfer truncation (a torn download usually yields a connection error or short body → mismatch). Adding mismatch to the retryable set is cheap and strictly more resilient. But — deterministic tampering would then burn retries before failing. 3 attempts × small files — negligible. Let me add the mismatch to retryable errors.

Actually — wait. Think: is a retry-on-mismatch SAFE? Yes: we only write after hash verification; retrying a download is idempotent and safe. Add `on PrewarmException` — hmm, but PrewarmException is also thrown for config-level problems (null releaseTag, missing pins) — those are thrown OUTSIDE fetchVerified (in prewarmPackage), so inside fetchVerified the only PrewarmException is the hash mismatch. Retry on it.

Also update the unit test? The corrupt-body test uses attempts: 2 — with retry-on-mismatch it'll retry twice then throw — still passes (throws PrewarmException). Fine either way, but let me assert the retry count to document the behavior... the existing test just expects a throw — still valid. I'll extend it slightly to count calls: mismatch → 2 attempts with attempts:2. Actually keep the test as-is (still green) and note the behavior. Hmm — cleaner to keep semantics simple: retry on mismatch. Update script, re-run tests.

Now — docs. Check docs/ci.md for where build-mobile leg hardening is documented, and the CHANGELOG convention.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

  guarantee ride the same `CompactionHostWiring` resolution as the CLI and
  app (`resolveExtensionCompactionWiring`); receipts are durable across
  panel attach/SW restart. Machine-review round 1: exact ladder pass
  counts, busy-matrix routing (`routeUserInput`) for panel text and second
  `/compact` during a pass, window settings from the ACTIVE stored source

===

  (CLI line mode prints directly, TUI re-prints after the banner, the app
  logs through its AppLog boot-notice seam). New `projectContext:` config
  section: `maxBytes` (default 32768) — `0` disables the section entirely
  and reads no files (fast boot); unknown keys are tolerated with a note.
  Leaf-first allocation is unchanged.

  download roulette for CMake. v1.0.619's `build-android` leg died at
  `:jni:configureCMakeDebug[arm64-v8a]` — the `:jni` module (transitive

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-2074): the daily-publish `play` leg no longer reds on a GitHub
  release-download brownout. Three build-mobile.yml Android jobs died in
  package:sqlite3's native-assets build hook with `Bad state: Hash of
  downloaded file libsqlite3.x64.android.so is bef140a1…` — the hook
  (released ≤3.9.1; the lockfile pins 3.7.0, the root floats 3.9.1)
  hashes the download WITHOUT honoring the HTTP status, so GitHub's 504
  page (a constant hash, upstream simolus3/sqlite3.dart#435) failed the
  pin check and the build exited 255. The assets themselves were intact;
  ci.yml had solved this exact class for itself on 2026-09-21 by caching
  `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared`, but build-mobile.yml never got the
  protection. Cure: new `scripts/sqlite3_hook_prewarm.dart` — derives the
  release tag + pinned hashes from the RESOLVED sqlite3 package (no
  second pin), gates on the HTTP status before hashing, bounded-retries
  with backoff, verifies SHA-256 before any cache write (tmp+rename),
  skips idempotently on a verified cache hit — wired as the
  `Native-assets hook cache` + `Pre-warm sqlite3 hook assets` steps in
  the two Android build jobs (both roots, `hooks-shared-mobile-` keys)
  and inside `assert-builtin-skills` for the root host asset (the step
  that failed first). Guard test `test/ci_sqlite3_hook_prewarm_guard_
  test.dart` pins the wiring (AC1-AC4); the script's byte-level behavior
  and the live hook-reuse layout are pinned in
  `test/scripts/sqlite3_hook_prewarm_test.dart`.

# Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

The play leg died in `package:sqlite3`'s native-assets build hook: it downloads prebuilt `libsqlite3` binaries from GitHub releases and hashes the response body **without honoring the HTTP status** (released 3.7.0 pinned by `flutter_app/pubspec.lock`; floating 3.9.1 at the root gained the check upstream but has no retry). A GitHub release-download brownout served 504 pages whose constant hash (`bef140a1…`, upstream simolus3/sqlite3.dart#435) failed the pinned-SHA-256 check → `build.dart returned with exit code: 255` on three jobs ~2 min apart. The release assets themselves were intact. ci.yml solved this exact class for itself on 2026-09-21 by caching `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared`; build-mobile.yml never received that protection.

### Fix

- `scripts/sqlite3_hook_prewarm.dart` (new): derives the release tag + pinned hashes from the **resolved** sqlite3 package (no second pin to drift), gates on HTTP status before hashing, bounded-retries with backoff (60s/attempt timeout), verifies SHA-256 before any cache write (tmp+rename), skips idempotently on a verified cache hit.
- `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`: `build-android` + `build-android-apks` restore an `actions/cache` (`hooks-shared-mobile-…`, both roots) **before** the assert gate, and pre-warm the flutter_app android assets after `flutter pub get`, before the build.
- `.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills/action.yml`: pre-warms the root host asset between `dart pub get` and the verify run (the step that failed first in the AAB job).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: gh-2074 entry under `## Unreleased`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/scripts/sqlite3_hook_prewarm_test.dart` — 23 unit tests: filename/cache-layout pins (live hook-reuse path), brownout retry, hash-gate-before-rename, corrupt-cache repair, multi-ABI seeding, loud errors.
- `test/ci_sqlite3_hook_prewarm_guard_test.dart` — YAML-level guard (AC1–AC4): script properties, both jobs' cache+pre-warm ordering, assert-action pre-warm, ci.yml regression pin. RED before the fix, GREEN after.
- Live verification: seeded all 4 android assets for the lockfile-pinned sqlite3-3.7.0 (the ticket's exact failing asset, hash `949965f0…` matches) and the root linux asset for 3.9.1; simulated brownouts over real HTTP — 504 → 3 attempts + `::error::` + **empty cache**; 200-with-error-page → hash gate refuses, cache stays empty.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **13497 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- The build-mobile iOS job rides a persistent self-hosted runner (its own `.dart_tool` persists across runs), so it was left untouched; same for the macOS legs — the action is reusable there if a brownout ever bites them.
- A failed pre-warm still fails the leg **loudly** (named URL + HTTP status) instead of the misleading hash-mismatch — worse-case behavior is honest, never silent.
- No new external dependencies: worst case (cold cache + brownout) is bounded retries against the same endpoint the hook hits today.

## gh-2074 — play leg fix complete

**Root cause**: `package:sqlite3`'s native-assets build hook downloads prebuilt `libsqlite3` binaries from GitHub releases and hashes the response body **without honoring the HTTP status** (the flutter_app lockfile pins 3.7.0; the root floats 3.9.1 which has the upstream status check but no retry). During a GitHub release-download brownout, the hook hashed GitHub's 504 page — a constant SHA-256 (`bef140a1…`) for every caller — failed the pinned-hash check, and exited 255 on three build-mobile.yml Android jobs. The assets themselves were intact. ci.yml had solved this exact class for itself on 2026-09-21 (hooks-shared cache); build-mobile.yml never received that protection.

**Fix** (branch `ai/gh-2074`, 4 commits above origin/main):
- New `scripts/sqlite3_hook_prewarm.dart` — derives the release tag + pinned hashes from the *resolved* sqlite3 package (no second pin), gates HTTP status before hashing, bounded-retries with backoff, verifies SHA-256 before any cache write, skips idempotently on a verified hit.
- `build-mobile.yml`: both failing Android jobs now restore an `actions/cache` of both hooks-shared roots **before** the assert gate and pre-warm the flutter_app android assets after pub-get, before the build.
- `assert-builtin-skills` action pre-warms the root host asset (the step that failed first).
- Companion guard test pins the wiring; script unit tests pin the byte-level behavior including the live hook-reuse layout.

**Verification highlights**: live E2E seeded the ticket's exact failing asset (`libsqlite3.x64.android.so` @ sqlite3-3.7.0, hash matches pin); simulated brownouts over real HTTP — 504 → 3 retries + loud `::error::` + empty cache; 200-with-error-page → hash gate refuses. Full suite: **13497 passed, 0 failed**.
